arrival: Lensy: look at what you've built, a partner chosen well or your own path held high, a fair home, your own footing. The turn to 'us', never losing the 'me'.
canvasPayoff: The canvas blooms into a warm home, door open: chairs at a shared table, a family of any shape in the window, a path to your own horizon, lit by eight stickers.

recap.bigTruth: You choose a partner on values, respect and how they handle conflict, not just sparks; lasting love is built daily through trust, repair and consent.
Marriage and children are one path, not the measure of a life; single, childfree or partnered, your worth is your own and the timeline is yours to set.
An equal home shares the whole load, the visible chores and the invisible mental load, and owning your share beats only helping; both partners' careers count.
Consent and respect live inside marriage too; abuse and coercive control are never your fault, and reaching for help is courage, not weakness.
You join a family, so you set kind boundaries, stand together as a team, and honour elders while keeping your own voice, with help if it ever turns harmful.
Fair money is open and planned, with both partners independent and informed, and controlling a partner's money is abuse, never just a division of labour.
Whether, when and how many children is yours to decide, free of pressure; fertility facts stay calm, and difficulty conceiving is common and no one's shame.
Family is built in many ways, adoption, ART, solo, queer, blended, all real; you go in informed about the barriers and live your family with pride.

playback.frame: Your A Life, Built constellation: eight stickers from a whole chapter of building an adult life, with a partner or on your own terms. Tap any star to revisit.
playback.celebrate: Eight stars in your sky, and a life you are building under them. Look at what you can do.

playback.frame: Remember this? Sort what makes a partner a deep green flag from what is only surface shine.
playback.celebrate: Still sharp, you read for what lasts, not what dazzles.

playback.frame: Remember the flip? Erase the old line and write the truer one.

myth.un: Helping out with chores means I share the home equally.
myth.re: Owning a share end-to-end, the planning and the remembering, is what equal really means.
myth.why: Helping waits to be asked; owning means carrying it, the planning and the remembering too.

playback.celebrate: You see the invisible load now, and you own your half.

playback.frame: Remember the call? A friend hints that things at home feel controlling and frightening.

options.text: Believe her, say it's not her fault, and share that help exists
options.consequence: You believe her, refuse blame, and point her to real help.

options.text: Tell her it's normal and to adjust
options.consequence: 'Just adjust' leaves her alone with it; believing her and naming that help exists is the supportive move.

playback.celebrate: You lead with belief and help, never blame.
playback.debrief: Belief, no blame, and a route to help. That's how you show up for someone.

playback.frame: Remember the pairs? Match each money tool to the job it does.
playback.celebrate: Open, planned, both independent, you've got the formula.

playback.frame: Remember the calm read? Swipe up for the honest, panic-free truth about fertility and age.
playback.cue: Fertility changes gradually with age, for women and men alike, with no sudden cut-off, and a weaponised clock helps no one.
playback.celebrate: You keep the facts calm and the clock un-weaponised.

playback.frame: Remember the words? A friend on a non-default path asks how you see their family.

yourLine.text: "Your family is every bit as real and worthy as anyone's, and I'm here for it."

playback.celebrate: Every family real, every one dignified, you say it without a blink.

reflect.prompt: Lensy: this chapter was about building a life, with someone or on your own terms. What part of building feels most like yours now?
reflect.affirm: Whatever you named, you are the one building it, and that is a quietly huge thing.

reflect.prompt: Lensy: a lot of this chapter was about staying yourself inside an 'us'. Where did that land for you?
options: I can build us without losing me
reflect.affirm: Building a shared life while staying whole is one of the hardest, finest skills there is.

reflect.prompt: Lensy: this chapter also said every path is valid, partnered, solo, childfree, many ways to family. How does that freedom sit with you?
reflect.affirm: Your life is yours to design; no single shape was ever the only real one.

reflect.prompt: Lensy: and you learned where the lines are, and where help lives, money, consent, safety. What feels different about knowing that?
options: I can spot what's not okay
reflect.affirm: Knowing the line and where help lives is what keeps a built life a safe one.

reflect.prompt: Lensy: Remember the freedom? One path is one path, not the measure of a life. Which truth from this chapter do you most want to carry forward?
options: My worth isn't my marital status
An equal home is a happier home
Help is a strength, not a weakness
reflect.affirm: Whatever you carry, you carry it as someone building a life on your own terms.

celebration.certificate: This certifies you a graduate of Chapter 7: A Life, Built. You choose on values, share the load, keep money fair, live consent at home. Stand tall.
celebration.stickerBook: All eight Chapter 7 stickers now glow in your A Life, Built constellation, crowned by a golden graduation star, every sticker since age 3 shining beneath it.

preview: Next, Chapter 8: Parenthood, the final chapter, for those who parent. Raise a child with the equality, consent and warmth you've carried all along.
share: Your call: if it feels right, tell someone you trust one thing you're proud of building, a fairer home, a clearer boundary, a choice of your own.
